title: Mother before Queen
hook: the hymn of a thousand names opens by calling the goddess Mother, before Queen or throne
carry: the goddess is mother before she is queen
tomorrow: the gods have run out of answers. then, a fire.

segments.voice: Yesterday, the hymn asked Kardama, the mud, to bring the lotus mother home: fortune rising clean from the mud. Today, a new hymn, made of names.
screen: `KARDAMA, BRING HER HOME.` · `FORTUNE RISING CLEAN FROM THE MUD.`

segments.voice: At seven in the morning she's Mom, hunting for a missing shoe. By nine she's Doctor, signing charts. At lunch a friend calls her by a nickname from college. At the temple an old aunty calls her beta, child. Same woman. Every name catches a different side of her, and nobody who loves her would pick just one. Now make that vast. The Lalita Sahasranama is a hymn made almost entirely of names for the goddess, one after another, line after line. Today, how it opens.
screen: `MOM AT SEVEN. DOCTOR BY NINE.` → `EVERY NAME, A DIFFERENT SIDE.` → `A HYMN MADE OF NAMES.`

segments.voice: Sahasranama means a thousand names, and Lalita is the goddess they belong to. Tradition places the hymn in the Brahmanda Purana, as a teaching the god Hayagriva gives to the sage Agastya. Some who worship her recite it name by name, at home or in temples. A hymn of names works differently from a story. There's no plot. Each name is a small window, and you look through one, then the next. Over the coming days the path will open a few of those windows, not all of them. So, the first three names, in paraphrase. Sri Mata: the auspicious Mother. Sri Maharajni: the great Queen. Srimat Simhasaneshvari: she who rules from the glorious lion throne. Notice the order. Mother first, before the crown, before the throne, before any of her power is named. Some teachers say that's the key to the whole hymn: whatever she is later, a warrior, a queen, the power behind the universe, she is that as a mother, and the one reciting comes to her as a child. Then the throne and the lion: royal names. And the very first sound is Sri, the word the Sri Sukta days were built on. Here is the teaching under the order. This is Shakta devotion, the worship of God as the Goddess, and its first move is to call the highest power Mother. You don't come to her as a subject with a petition. You come as her child. That's why so many Hindus simply say Ma, at the temple, at the home shrine, under their breath in a hard week. Not a lesser name. The first one.
screen: `A HYMN MADE OF NAMES.` · `SRI MATA, THE MOTHER.` · `GREAT QUEEN, ON THE LION THRONE.` · `YOU COME AS HER CHILD.` · then, large: `MOTHER BEFORE QUEEN.`

segments.voice: Try what devotees do with this hymn: say the first three names slowly, Sri Mata, Sri Maharajni, Srimat Simhasaneshvari, with folded hands, or a flower or a pinch of kumkum for each if you have a shrine. Then say only the first one a few more times, and rest there. If you don't pray, say the meanings in English, Mother, great Queen, the one on the lion throne, and notice which one feels closest.
The Lalita Sahasranama. A hymn of names for the goddess Lalita, which opens Sri Mata, the Mother, before Queen or throne.
Your line: the goddess is mother before she is queen. Sri Mata comes first. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1100 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: OUT OF THE FIRE, A GODDESS.`

howItsDone: Some Hindus, especially in Shakta and Sri Vidya communities, recite the Lalita Sahasranama in full at home or in temples, sometimes offering a flower or a pinch of kumkum with each name.

Lalita Sahasranama.meaning: a hymn of a thousand names for the goddess Lalita

Hayagriva.meaning: the god who gives the hymn's teaching, says tradition

Agastya.meaning: the sage who receives the teaching

Sri Mata.meaning: the auspicious Mother, the hymn's first name

beta.meaning: Hindi for child, said with affection

sources.ref: Lalita Sahasranama, names 1–3 (Brahmanda Purana, Lalitopakhyana, as traditionally placed)

notes: Names 1–3 paraphrased: śrīmātā, śrīmahārājñī, śrīmatsiṃhāsaneśvarī. Confirm glosses.

'Sahasranama means a thousand names' is the title's meaning; the count is not otherwise asserted. Tradition places the hymn in the Brahmanda Purana as Hayagriva's teaching to Agastya; attributed to tradition. Confirm.
'The lion carries an echo of the fierce goddess the path met in the Devi Mahatmya' is an interpretive link (Durga's lion), offered lightly; confirm or cut.
'Some teachers say that's the key to the whole hymn' (Mother before Queen) is interpretive; confirm it is fair to the commentarial tradition (e.g., Bhaskararaya).
howItsDone mentions Shakta and Sri Vidya communities and kumkum offerings with each name (kumkumarchana); confirm wording.
The meaning of the name Lalita ('she who plays', 'the lovely one') is not given aloud.
